items.title: North American robot orders increase 25 percent in third quarter of 2026
items.summary: North American companies ordered 10,989 robots valued at $723.5 million in the third quarter of 2026, marking a 25 percent increase in both units and value compared to the previous year. This growth was driven by strong demand across various sectors, including Automotive OEMs, Semiconductors/Electronics, and Life Sciences. Collaborative robot orders also saw a significant 56 percent increase during the quarter. The overall trend suggests a diversified and strengthening robotics market across different industries. Despite some economic uncertainties, the market enters the final quarter of 2026 with positive momentum.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, North American robot orders increased by twenty-five percent in the third quarter of 2026. This report details the significant growth observed in robot procurement across North American companies during that period. North American companies ordered ten thousand nine hundred eighty-nine robots valued at seven hundred twenty-three point five million dollars, representing a twenty-five percent increase in both units and total value compared to the prior year. This expansion was fueled by robust demand within several key sectors, specifically Automotive Original Equipment Manufacturers, Semiconductors and Electronics, and Life Sciences. Furthermore, orders for collaborative robots experienced a substantial fifty-six percent increase during the same quarter. This data indicates a broad and intensifying market for robotics across diverse industrial applications. Positive momentum is entering the final quarter of 2026 for the sector.

items.title: BMW and Embotech move ‘1 million vehicles using automated driving technology’
items.summary: BMW Group and Embotech have successfully moved one million vehicles using automated driving technology across four production sites in the UK and Germany. This achievement demonstrates the scalability of Automated Driving In-Plant within the BMW Group's production network. The solution supports approximately 3,500 vehicle movements daily with over 99.5 percent availability. Embotech provides the AI-based software and safety architecture necessary for this reliable operation. This deployment showcases how the technology enhances production efficiency, flexibility, and safety.

items.title: AGIBOT Livestreams Six G2 Robots in a 24-Hour Convenience Store Challenge
items.summary: Six AGIBOT G2 robots participate in a 24-hour livestream challenge set in a convenience store environment. The challenge, running from November 2nd to 3rd, involves tasks like stocking shelves, making coffee, and greeting customers during rush periods. The broadcast aims to provide an extended view of the robots operating amidst human activity. The livestream offers insight into how the robots manage routine variations and interruptions during continuous work. Complete details on task success and autonomy will be assessed based on intervention and recovery during the event.

items.title: What battery technology will power the next generation of humanoid robots?
items.summary: Current humanoid robots primarily use NMC-based lithium-ion batteries, balancing energy density with necessary performance criteria. Future developments are exploring solid-state batteries, which offer higher energy density and improved safety by replacing liquid electrolytes. Lithium-sulfur cells present an alternative with high theoretical energy density but face challenges with cycle life and fast charging limitations. Improvements to NMC cathodes, by increasing nickel content, can also boost performance while reducing cobalt use. Ultimately, the transition to advanced battery technologies will be driven by the need for higher energy density, safety, and longevity in humanoid applications.
items.audio_script: From Robotics & Automation News, "What battery technology will power the next generation of humanoid robots?". This report examines the battery technologies poised to power future humanoid robots, focusing on advancements in energy density, safety, and longevity. Current humanoid robots predominantly utilize NMC-based lithium-ion batteries, which currently balance energy density requirements with operational performance criteria. Future research is focusing heavily on solid-state batteries, which promise increased energy density and enhanced safety through the elimination of liquid electrolytes. Alternatively, lithium-sulfur cells are being explored for their high theoretical energy density, although challenges remain regarding cycle life and charging speeds. Furthermore, adjustments to NMC cathode compositions, specifically increasing nickel content, offer a pathway to improve performance while mitigating cobalt usage. The progression toward these advanced battery systems is necessitated by the demand for greater energy density and improved safety in humanoid applications. This transition signals a necessary technological shift in energy storage for the advancement of humanoid robotics.

items.title: Interview with TorqueAGI founder: ‘Most robot AI is a language or vision model with robot data added to it’
items.summary: TorqueAGI develops a World-Reasoning Model for industrial robots and heavy machinery by incorporating physics and geometry into a spatio-temporal architecture. This approach allows machines to adapt to changes and learn new tasks from minimal demonstrations using existing customer operational data. The model differs from vision-language-action models by building reasoning directly on spatial-temporal graphs rather than solely relying on large demonstration sets. Integration focuses on the model's intelligence, leaving hardware and sensor integration as the responsibility of the machine manufacturers. The Sovereign Physical AI architecture emphasizes running models locally to ensure operational autonomy, control, and accountability for industrial equipment.

items.title: Solving the Interconnect Challenge in Modern Robotics: How 3M Is Engineering for Motion, Density, and Uptime
items.summary: Robotics interconnects face challenges related to signal integrity, mechanical durability, and board space due to increasing system complexity. 3M addresses these issues with a portfolio of solutions focusing on motion, density, and uptime. Their offerings include high-flex cable assemblies with validated cycle life, fast IDC termination methods, and reduced-pitch connectors to save board space. Furthermore, 3M provides solutions that enhance reliability against vibration and manage EMI/crosstalk in dense wiring. These interconnect strategies offer engineers validated options to improve the reliability and performance of next-generation robotic hardware.

This story details how 3M addresses challenges in robotics interconnects related to signal integrity, mechanical durability, and board space through specific engineering solutions. 3M’s portfolio addresses these issues with high-flex cable assemblies possessing validated cycle life, fast IDC termination methods, and reduced-pitch connectors designed to conserve board space. Additionally, the company provides solutions that enhance reliability against vibration and manage electromagnetic interference and crosstalk within dense wiring configurations. These interconnect strategies offer engineers validated options to improve the reliability and performance of next-generation robotic hardware. This work provides validated pathways for advancing the performance and dependability of future robotic systems.

items.title: Meta reportedly builds Max humanoid prototype with Fourier
items.summary: Meta has reportedly built a humanoid prototype named Max in collaboration with the Chinese robotics company Fourier. This prototype is intended as a physical embodiment of Meta’s Muse agent, focusing on household tasks. The robot was developed in about three months and weighs approximately 106 pounds (48 kg). Meta plans to build a second version but has no plans to sell these units, positioning it as an internal development platform. The partnership leverages Fourier's expertise in robotics hardware to support Meta's AI and software development.

items.title: RoboParty launches RP1 humanoid with open hardware and software
items.summary: RoboParty launched the RP1 humanoid, an open hardware and software research platform with 24 or 30 actuated degrees of freedom. Researchers have full access to mechanical designs, actuators, firmware, control algorithms, and learning tools to modify the robot. The platform supports research in gait, balance control, and embodied AI through simulation and physical deployment. It includes built-in capabilities for walking, fall recovery, and motion tracking, along with tools like VR teleoperation. This open approach allows teams to inspect and adjust all components for practical debugging advantages.

The demonstration only shows an interaction and does not explain the underlying technology or an imminent customer release. The company is still awaiting customer deliveries for the NEO robots, which are targeted for 2026.

items.title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
items.summary: Imitation learning policies often fail in real-world robotic manipulation because conventional optimization signals do not align with actual success. Evaluation of 281 policies using real-robot trials on grasping and insertion revealed that observation and action representations were dominant factors. Specific representation choices, such as region-of-interest cropping for point-cloud policies, significantly improved performance. Furthermore, absolute action prediction rather than relative prediction boosted insertion success for vision-language-action policies. Representation choices are critical determinants of imitation learning performance, though offline metrics alone are insufficient.

items.title: FlapSim: A Composable MuJoCo Simulation Platform and Reduced-Order Aerodynamic Model Hierarchy for Flapping-Wing Robotics
items.summary: FlapSim is a modular MuJoCo simulation platform designed for flapping-wing robotics by combining robot descriptions, wing geometry, and composable aerodynamic models. It evaluates five reduced-order aerodynamic configurations against a high-fidelity $50\,\mu\text{s}$ blade-element reference across various flight conditions. Incorporating multirate synchronization, inflow/gust coupling, and harmonic synthesis significantly improves simulation fidelity. The results indicate that timing, inflow, geometry, and harmonic representation are critical factors in the accuracy-computation tradeoff of the reduced-order model. Ultimately, the work characterizes the necessary trade-offs for simulating flapping-wing dynamics effectively.

items.title: Confidence-Modulated Safety Filtering for End-to-End Policies
items.summary: End-to-end policies require safety filters, which typically maintain a fixed level of conservativeness regardless of the policy's actual competence. The authors propose a method to modulate this filtering based on the policy's confidence level at runtime. Inside the operational design domain (ODD), high confidence allows for performance gains, while low confidence introduces a margin to flag where the filter may be failing. This approach combines the strengths of both permissive and conservative filters. Preliminary simulations suggest this confidence-modulated filtering effectively combines these filter types.

items.title: STAR: Steering Action Representations during Inference
items.summary: Vision-language-action models show strong capabilities in robotic manipulation but action representations near the output do not fully preserve task-relevant visual grounding. STAR introduces a training-free inference method for pre-trained VLAs by applying an exponential moving average over late-layer residual updates. This method allows later action representations to inherit object-aware update directions from earlier layers without model updates. STAR also uses proprioceptive states to adjust mixing strength, employing conservative mixing when execution dynamics change rapidly. Experiments demonstrate that STAR improves late-layer object awareness and increases average task success rates by 4.0 percentage points.

items.title: Contact Imitation Interface: Transferring Dexterous Skills by Showing How Contact Unfolds
items.summary: A framework called Contact Imitation Interface (CIMI) is presented to transfer dexterous skills from human demonstrations to robots. CIMI utilizes contact-grounded demonstration and learning interfaces to address challenges in producing robot-transferable actions. The demonstration interface combines shared contact geometry and fingertip RGB views with contact-alignment-first retargeting. The learning interface employs a hierarchical policy that predicts contact-surface trajectories and coordinates finger/wrist commands. This method improves the mean final-stage success by at least 50 percentage points across six hand-task pairs.

items.title: Veloxity: Towards Memory-Safe UAV Embedded Firmware using the Rust Programming Language
items.summary: Veloxity is an open-source, memory-safe embedded UAV autopilot developed using the Rust programming language. It aims to address the lack of memory-safe practices in the aerospace domain for UAV firmware. The project provides a minimal, modular foundation to lower the barrier for using memory-safe languages in modern ecosystems. Performance comparisons with C++ autopilots in simulation and flight tests demonstrate functional parity. These results suggest that memory-safe languages are viable for reliable and performant autonomous aerospace systems.

items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
items.summary: End-to-end self-driving models lack transparency despite strong planning performance. Mechanistic interpretability is applied using Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on a single-camera path planning model's internal activations. Unsupervised clustering of SAE latents reveals interpretable structures related to route intent, speed, and braking, accurately recovering route intent. These SAE features are found to be visually grounded and systematically respond to scene changes. Finally, using these representations in an adapter improved trajectory selection error, confirming their utility for interpretability.

items.title: A Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter for Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Navigation
items.summary: Safe navigation for heterogeneous multi-robot teams is complicated by differing braking and turning capabilities and the need for coordinated control actions. The Capability-Aware Backup-Recoverability Filter (CA-BRF) is proposed to address this by ensuring navigation actions preserve access to certified recovery maneuvers. It constructs backup-recoverable sets based on pairwise safety and robot constraints to define capability-dependent recovery certificates. CA-BRF filters candidate controls by selecting admissible interpolations, preserving recoverability while satisfying all pairwise recovery conditions. This method establishes recursive feasibility and safety for the system during complex interactions involving up to 30 heterogeneous robots.
